He put one part of the force into the hands of Joab, the second company he gave to Abishai, Joab's brother, the son of Zeruiah, and the third company he gave to Ittai the Gittite. And King David said to the people: "I too will go out with you!"

The people answered and said to him: "You shall not go out with us. If we are put to flight, there will be no one to keep up our courage. And if half of us are killed, there will be no one to comfort us, for from then on part of this land would be taken from us by these thousands of people [?]. It is better and best for us that you stay in the city as the support of our help, and call out to us!"
The king answered and said: "It is good; do whatever is pleasing to you." And the king came and stood at one side of the gates, and the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

And the king commanded Joab, Abishai and Ittai the Gittite, his commanders, and said: "Take care, be careful, spare my boy Absalom!" And all the people heard the king's command to the commanders concerning Absalom.
And all the people went out and drew up in battle order on the plain, face to face before all the people of Israel; and the battle was fought in the forest of Mahanaim.
And the people of Israel were given over to defeat before the servants of David, and there was a great slaughter among the people on that day, and twenty thousand men of the people of Israel fell.
And the people of Israel were scattered through the whole forest, and more of the people of Israel were destroyed by the forest than by the edge of the sword.

And Absalom stood out conspicuously before the people. He was riding his mount, and as he passed beneath a young tree in his flight, the branches of the tree caught hold of his head, and he was left hanging from the tree between heaven and earth, and his mount went out from under his legs.
And a man saw it, came and told Joab, saying: "Look, I saw Absalom hanging from a tree."

And Joab said to the man who was telling him: "You really saw him hanging from the tree? Then why did you not kill him and pin him to the ground right there? I would have given you fifty shekels this very day."

The man answered Joab and said: "Even if you gave me a thousand weights of silver, I would never have laid my hands on the king's son, for we heard with our own ears when he commanded you, Abishai and Ittai, saying: 'Take care, I beg you, of my boy Absalom!'

"And now how could I have done such a thing, or brought such lawlessness upon my own head? I know that the matter would not have been hidden from the king, and you would not truly have stood up for me before him."

Joab said to him: "For that word I will show you right now, before your eyes!" And Joab took three darts in his hand and thrust them into Absalom's heart while he was still alive and hanging from the tree.
Immediately the servants, Joab's [?] companions, surrounded him, struck Absalom, pinned him to the ground and killed him.
And at once they blew the trumpet and called the people back, so that no one would pursue the Israelites any longer, for Joab had pity on the people of Israel.

And Joab had Absalom taken up and had him thrown into a cleft in the ground in the forest, a great pit, and he raised over it a great heap of stones. And all the people of Israel fled, each to his own place.

While Absalom was still alive, he had taken a pillar and set it up for himself in the King's Valley, for he said: "Since I have no son to keep my name in remembrance, let this be called the Hand of Absalom." And from then on it has been called the Hand of Absalom to this day.
And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said to Joab: "Let me run and go and bring the king the good news that the Lord has carried out a judgment of vengeance for him against the hand of his enemies."
Joab said to him: "You are not the man to bring news on this day, and you shall not tell this message to the king, for the king's son is dead. If you are to bring any news, bring it on another day!"
Joab said to Cushi: "Go and tell the king what you have seen!" And Cushi bowed down before Joab and ran off.

And Ahimaaz son of Zadok spoke to Joab once more and said to him: "What does it matter if I run after Cushi too?" And Joab said to him: "Why do you need to run, my son? This news will bring you no profit, that you should run!"
Ahimaaz said to him: "Whatever happens, let me run." Then he said to him: "Run!" And Ahimaaz ran by the inner road, in the direction of Cushi [?].

And David was sitting between the two gates. And the young man who was the watchman went up by the roof [?] of the gate to the tower. He raised his eyes and looked, and there was a man running before his eyes.

The watchman called out and said: "A man is running fast from the direction of the storehouse [?]!" The king said to him: "If he is alone, there is good news in his mouth!" And he kept coming and drew near.
Then the watchman saw another man running. The watchman called out and said: "Look, another man is running. He is bringing news too!"
The watchman spoke and said: "I can see how the first one runs, and it looks like the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok!" And the king said: "He is a good man, and he must be bringing good news!"

And Ahimaaz came before the king and said: "Life and peace!" And he bowed down before him with his face to the ground and said: "Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who has struck down the men who raised themselves up in enmity against my lord the king!"

The king spoke and said to him: "Is my boy Absalom alive?" Ahimaaz answered and said to him: "I heard the sound of an outcry after I set out, when Joab sent me, and I do not know what happened there."
The king said: "Step aside!" And he moved over and stood behind him.
And just then Cushi arrived and said: "Rejoice, my lord the king, for today the Lord has judged in vengeance for you against the hands of all your enemies!"
The king said to Cushi: "Is the young man Absalom alive?" Cushi answered and said to him: "May all your enemies, and all who have risen up against you to do evil, become like that young man!"

And the king wept, and he went up to the upper chamber over the gate. He wept greatly, and as he wept he said: "My son Absalom, my son! If only someone had killed me in place of your death, my son Absalom!"
They told Joab, saying to him: "Do you know that the king is weeping and mourning for Absalom?"
And the victory of that day turned into mourning for all the people, when the people heard that day that the king was weeping and mourning for his son Absalom.
And the people were ashamed to enter the city, like people who have been defeated and put to flight in battle.
And the king sat with his head bowed and covered. He wept with a loud voice and said: "My son Absalom, Absalom, my son!"

And Joab went in to the king and said to him: "Why have you put to shame the faces of these servants of yours, who saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, and of your wives and concubines?

Today you have shown the people that it is as if they love those who hate you and hate those who love you. Today you have shown that neither princes nor servants mean anything to you. But know this for yourself: it would be worse if Absalom were alive and we had all perished before you, because he was pleasing to you in your eyes.

But now get up and speak to the hearts of these servants of yours, for these men have sworn an oath by the Lord that if you do not go out to meet the people, no one will stay with you this night. And know this for yourself: this will be worse for you than all the troubles that have come upon you from your youth until now."

And the king got up, dressed, went out, and sat at the gates of the city. All the people heard that the king had come out and was sitting at the gates. And all the people came to meet the king at the gates of the city. But the Israelites fled, each to his own place.

All the tribes of Israel grumbled and said to one another: "King David saved us from the hands of our enemies. He rescued us from the hands of the foreigners. And now we are fugitives from his land and from his kingdom because of Absalom.

And Absalom, whom we anointed king over us, has been killed in battle. So now why are you silent and sitting still, and not turning back to your lord the king?" And these words of all the Israelites reached the king.
And King David sent to the high priests Zadok and Abiathar and said: "Say to the elders of the people: Why do you delay to bring back your lord the king?
Are you not my brothers? You are flesh of my flesh and bone of my bones. Why do you delay to bring the king back to his house?
And say this to Amasa: Are you not my bone and my flesh? May God do this to me, and add more to it, if you are not commander of my army in place of Joab for all the days of your life!"
And Amasa turned the hearts of all the men of Judah to obedience, as if they were one man. They sent to the king and said: "Return to us, together with all your servants!"
And the king returned to them and came as far as the bank of the river Jordan. And all the people of Judah came as far as Gilgal to meet the king, so that they could bring him across the river.
And Shimei son of Gera, son of Jemini, the Choranite [?], hurried and came, and he came with the men of Judah to meet David.

And a thousand other men from the house of Benjamin were with him, and Ziba, the servant of the house of Saul, with his fifteen sons, his wife, his manservant and his maidservant; and they brought them down to the Jordan for the king,
to serve him, to bring the king across the river, and to do what was pleasing in his eyes. And Shimei son of Gera fell on his face before the king just as he was crossing the river Jordan,

and said to the king: "Let not my lord the king take to heart the iniquity that your servant committed against you, the sin he committed against you on the day when my lord the king went out of Jerusalem.
I myself know that your servant sinned against you, and now I have come first of all the house of Joseph to present myself before the king."
Abishai son of Zeruiah (Georgian: "Sharoel") began to speak and said: "Even if there were nothing else, for this alone he deserves death, because Shimei dared to curse the Lord's anointed!"

David answered and said: "What do I have to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that today you become plotters of evil against me in hostility? Far be it from me that anyone should be put to death in Israel! Or do you not know that today I am king over Israel?"
And the king said to Shimei: "Do not be afraid, for you shall not die!" And the king swore an oath to Shimei.

And Mephibosheth (Georgian: Memphibal), son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came down to meet the king. He had not washed his feet, nor trimmed his nails, nor cleaned his nose, nor washed his clothes from the day the king went out of his house until the day he came back in peace to Jerusalem, when he came to meet him.
And the king said to him: "Why did you not come out with us, Mephibosheth?"

And Mephibosheth said: "My lord the king, my servant abandoned me when I said to him, 'Set me on my mount [?] and I will go with the king,' because I could not go with you without the mount [?], for your servant is lame.
Moreover, he slandered me before my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of the Lord; do what is good in the sight of God.

For my father's house was nothing else but men who all deserved death before our lord the king; yet you placed your servant among those who eat at the king's table. And now from whom did this justice come to me, if not from you?" And he said this, crying aloud, before the king.
The king said: "Why do you keep multiplying your words? What is this you have said? Now go and take a share of that field of yours."
Mephibosheth answered and said to the king: "Since I have seen the king return in peace to his house, let all of it, [?] the half, be his!"
And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and crossed the river Jordan with the king, to escort him from the Jordan.
And Barzillai was a man old in days, about eighty years old. He had provided for the king when the king was encamped in the wilderness, for he was very rich.
The king answered Barzillai and said: "If it pleases you, come with me, and your old age will be provided for with honour in Jerusalem."
Barzillai said to the king: How many more days of my life are left, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

For I am a man of eighty years, and today I can no longer tell good from evil. Can I still taste what I eat or drink? Can I still hear the voices of singers? So why should your servant be a burden to my lord the king?
Your servant will go with you across the waters only a little way, O king. So why do you give me toil as a reward for my service?

Let your servant go back to his own place, so that I may go and die there in my own city and be buried in my father's tomb. But let my son Chimham go with my lord the king, and do for him whatever is pleasing in your eyes!
The king answered him and said: So be it. Let your son Chimham come with me, and I will do for him whatever seems pleasing in my eyes, and I will do for him everything you ask of me.

And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king had also crossed and was standing on the bank of the river. And the king kissed Barzillai on the face and blessed him, and Barzillai went back to his home.
And the king crossed the Jordan and went to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed with him. And all the people of Judah came with him, and part of the people of Israel.

And all the people of Israel gathered and said to him: What is this? Your brothers, the men of Judah, have stolen you away as if by theft and brought you across the river Jordan, you and your household and all your people!

The men of Judah answered the men of Israel: Because the king is close kin to us. But why are you angry and grieved over this? Have we eaten [?] or drunk anything of the king's? Have we received any gift from him, or has he taken any portion from us?

The men of Israel answered and said: We are ten times closer to the king than you are, and we have more of the right of the firstborn with him than you do, and we are closer to him than you are. So why have you treated us with contempt? Was bringing back the king not our right rather than yours? And the words of the men of Judah were harsher than the words of the men of Israel.

And a worthless man happened to be there (literally, "a man born of lawlessness"), whose name was Sheba son of Bichri, a [?] (Benjaminite?). He blew the trumpet and said: We have no portion in David, and no inheritance in the son of Jesse! Go home, every man of Israel, each to his own dwelling!
And all the Israelites who were with the king left and followed Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah went with the king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

And David came and went into his house in Jerusalem. King David took the ten concubines he had left to keep the house and put them in a house [?] to be kept under guard, and he gave them provisions, but he himself did not go in to them. And they were kept shut up and ate the provisions of widowhood until the day they died.
And the king said to Amasa: Summon all the people of Judah to come within three days, and you yourself be here!
And Amasa went to summon them, and he did not [?] delay [?] the time that David had ordered him.

David began to speak to Amasa and said to him: "Surely Sheba, the son of Bedad, will now do us three more harm by his wickedness than Absalom did? Now take the people of your lord with you and overtake him! Otherwise he may find fortified cities and take refuge in them from us."
And David commanded that all the people should go with Abishai, along with Joab, the Pelethites, the Cherethites and all the mighty men of Israel, and they pursued Sheba, the son of Bedad.

They had arrived and camped by the great stone that was on the hill. Amasa came and stood in front of them. Joab was clothed in a coat of mail, and over it he had girded on a two-edged [?] sword, and it had slipped out of its sheath.
And Joab put his hand on Amasa's neck, as if to kiss him.

Amasa did not take care to guard himself from Joab's sword. Joab struck Amasa above the stomach and spilled out his bowels, and he did not strike him again, for his spirit departed at that very moment. And Joab and Amasa pursued Sheba, the son of Bedad.
And a man came and stood over Amasa, one of Joab's servants, and said: "What will you answer David?"

"For look, Amasa is dead and lies soaked in blood in the middle of the road, and every man who comes along that road goes up to Amasa." When they heard these words, they lifted Amasa, moved him away from the road, and covered him with a garment, because everyone who came along that road would stop over him.
And when they had moved him away from the road, all the people from then on followed in Joab's track, pursuing Sheba, the son of Bedad.
And they came through all the tribes of Israel, and to Sabeth [?] and Beth-maacah. All those cities gathered and came to pursue him.

They came and surrounded him in Abel-beth-maacah. They raised wall upon wall against the city, and all of Joab's people surrounded and enclosed it, and they brought the city to the point of being taken.
And a wise woman called out from the wall and said: "Listen, listen to me, you who are besieging this city, and tell Joab to come closer so that I may speak to him!"

And when Joab came close to the wall, the woman began to speak to Joab and said to him: "Are you Joab?" And he said: "I am!" The woman said to him: "Listen to these words of your handmaid!" Joab said to her: "I am listening, speak!"

And she said to him: "Let your handmaid speak. It was said as a proverb by those of old: 'Let them ask a question in Abel, and they will fail in Dan' [?]—which the faithful of Israel laid down, saying: 'Let them ask a question in Abel, and so they will come to an end.'"

"Now I am the peace and the steadfastness of the Israelites, and now you have come to destroy a city that is a mother of the cities of Israel. Why, then, are you swallowing up the inheritance of the Lord?"
Joab answered and said to her: "Far be it from me that I should swallow it up or bring any destruction on it!"

"It is not as you say. But one man, Sheba, the son of Bedad, from Mount Ephraim, has fled into the city there. He lifted up his hands and rose in rebellion against King David. Hand over him alone to me, and I will go away from that city of yours." The woman answered and said to him: "Now look, while you stand there, his head will be thrown down to you from the wall."

And the woman went there into the city and spoke her words of wisdom to the people and the citizens. And they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bedad and threw it down to Joab. And Joab ordered the trumpet to be blown, and he stopped the fighting against that city. And all the people scattered, each one to his own place, and Joab went back to the king there in Jerusalem.
And Joab was over the whole army of Israel, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the clay-workers and over the mighty men.
And Ezedran was the tribute collector, and Shaphan son of Akital was the recorder.
And Sosak was chief of the scribes, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
And Iodae and Etheran served as priests who stood before David.

And there was a great famine in the days of David for three years, year after year. And David inquired of the Lord, and the Lord said to David: "This famine is because of Saul and his lawlessness, and because of his house, for he slaughtered the Gibeonites."

And King David summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. For the Gibeonites were not from the sons of Israel; they were from the remnant of the Amorites. The sons of Israel had sworn not to destroy them, but Saul had set his heart on slaughtering them out of his zeal for the Israelites and for Judah.
And David said: "What shall I do for you? How shall I make atonement for this curse, so that you will bless me and the inheritance of the Lord?"

And the Gibeonites said: "We do not need gold or silver, and the sons of Israel are not liable to death. Our case is against the house of Saul." David said to them: "What do you want? What shall I do for you?"
They said to David: "The man who destroyed us and dishonored us, let us destroy him and wipe him out, so that he does not remain [?] before our eyes within the borders of Israel!"
"And now give us seven men from among his sons, and through them we will make atonement to the Lord on Saul's hill as an offering to the Lord." And the king said: "I will give them."
King David was anxious to spare Memphilbal, the son of Jonathan son of Saul, because of the oath of the Lord, the oath that had been sworn between David and Jonathan.

And the king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul, Aki and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Merab daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Iezrai son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

And he handed them over to the Gibeonites. They took them and exposed [?] them before the Lord. Those seven sons of his fell there on the mountain and perished at the beginning of the [?], in the days of the barley harvest.

And Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, took sackcloth and ashes and spread it out for herself on the rock in the days of the barley harvest, until God poured down rain from heaven. And she guarded them, and no bird of the sky touched them by day, and no beast of the earth by night, and they decomposed and rotted away right there.
And Dan son of Joash, who was one of the descendants of the giants, came against them. And they told David everything that Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, had done.

And David went and took the bones of Saul and of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-gilead. They had stolen the bones from the wall of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hung them on the day they slew and destroyed Saul and all his people at Gilboa.
And David brought the bones of Saul and of Jonathan his son up from there, and he also gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.

And he buried the bones of Saul and their bones in the land of Benjamin, near the tomb of Kish his father. They did everything according to the king's command, and only then did God show mercy to the land and lift their curse from it.

After all this the Philistines were continually at war with the Israelites. And David came with the people to the contest of battle against the Philistines. And when David saw Dadue, son of Joash, in his might, he grew faint,
for this Dadue was of the race of the giants. The weight of his spearhead was three hundred shekels of bronze, and his sword was at his waist, and he intended to attack David and kill him.

At that very moment Abishai, son of Zeruiah, rushed in between them, struck and killed the Philistine, and rescued David. And David's people gathered together and made a vow and swore an oath that David should no longer go out with them to battle, so that the lamp of Israel would not be put out.
After this there was another battle against the Philistines at Gaze. Then Boko the Kitite slew the bands of the Philistines who had gathered and come up against them.
Then there was another battle with the Philistines at Horoth, and Elhanan, son of Ialdin, son of Elemie, killed Golnan the Gittite. The shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam.

Then once more there was the contest of battle, a battle against the Philistines. And there was a man there of [?], and the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet were six on each, twenty-four in number. He too was of the race of the giants.
And he came out and stood between the two battle lines and taunted the people of Israel. There went out against him [?]
These four were born of the race of the giants who lived in Gath, of the house of Rapha. And David destroyed them by means of his people.
And then David spoke this word of song before the Lord on the day when the Lord delivered him from the hands of his enemies and from the hands of Saul.
And he said: I will love you, O Lord, my strength! The Lord is the one who strengthens me in my affliction, and may he deliver me,
God my Creator, and I will take shelter in him, for he is my coat of mail and the horn of my salvation. He alone is my refuge and my deliverer, and he delivered me from the lawless.
With praise I will call on the Lord, and he will deliver me from my enemies!
The terrors of the waters surrounded me, and violent torrents engulfed me!
The bonds of hell surrounded me, and the snares of death overtook me!
In my distress I called on the Lord, and I cried out to my God. From his holy temple he heard my voice! My cry reached his ears!
He looked, and the earth shook and trembled, and the foundations of the mountains were shaken. They cried out, for God was angry with them!
Smoke went up in his wrath, and fire blazed out from his mouth, and sparks were scattered from him!
And he bowed the heavens and came down; mist was beneath his feet!
He mounted the cherubim and flew; he was lifted up on the wings of the winds.
He set darkness as a covering for himself all around him, his dwelling and the coverings [?] of the clouds, clouds of wind over the waters!
With brightness they went before him, with hail and with sparks of fire!
And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave forth his voice!
He sent forth sling-stones and scattered them, and he made his lightnings flash, mingled with hail, and confounded [?] them!
They were terrified at the spreading out of the sea; the foundations of the world were laid bare at the wrath of the Lord and at the breath of his anger!
He sent from on high and took me up out of the waters!
He delivered me from the might of my enemies and from those who hate me, for they were stronger than I!
They came upon me on the day of my destruction, and the Lord was my helper!
And he brought me out into a broad place; he rescued me, because he desired me.
May the Lord reward me according to my righteousness, and according to the purity of my hands, my glory before his eyes!
With the merciful you were merciful, and with the holy man you were holy, and with the blameless you were blameless!
And with the chosen you were chosen, and with the crooked you were crooked!
For you, O Lord, saved the lowly people, and you brought low the eyes of the proud!
For you lit my lamp, O Lord, my Lord, and you lit up my darkness!
Through you I ran armed, and through my God I go [?] like a [?]!
God is holy, and his way is blameless! The command of the Lord is firm and refined, and he himself is a refuge for those who fear him!
For who is God besides the Lord? Or who is Creator except our God?
God, who armed me with strength and filled my ways with righteousness!
Make my feet firm and set me upon the heights!
He who trains my hands for battle, and my bow did not grow weak in my arms!
Arm me with the armour of salvation, and increase humility in me; and your right hand took hold of me, and your teaching set me upright!
You made my steps wide beneath me, and I did not grow weak in my places! Wants [?] astonished [?] me, and those who attacked me could not stand against me!
I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and I did not turn back from them until they were consumed, and I finished them off on the way!
I crushed them, and they did not rise again, and they fell under my feet.
He girded me with strength and joy for battle against them, and I shattered those who had risen up against me!
And he gave my enemies into my hands; I trampled the necks of my enemies!
They cried out, and there was no one who would save them by the Lord God, and he did not hear them.
I scattered them like dust before the wind, and like the mud of the streets I ground them down!
He delivered me from the oppression of the people; he set me as a light to the nations; a people whom I did not know served me.
At the hearing of the ear they submitted to me; sons lied to me.
And strangers rescued me and delivered me from bonds.
The Lord lives, and blessed is my Creator, and exalted be God my Saviour!
Mighty is the Lord God, who avenged me and humbled the peoples under me.
He rescued me from the wrath of my enemies; he lifted me up from my place; he guarded me from lawless men!
Therefore I will confess you among the nations, O Lord, and I will call to mind the name of the Lord!
Magnify the salvation of his king, show mercy to his anointed, to David from generation to generation, and to his descendants forever and ever!
These are the last words of David. Faithful is David, the son of Jesse, and faithful is the man whom God raised up, the anointed of Jacob; and beautiful is this song of Israel.
For the Spirit of the Lord spoke this, and the words of his mouth were on my tongue.
And the God of Jacob said, the Creator of Israel spoke concerning me: He set me as ruler over men, to rule over them with justice and the fear of God.
Like the morning star at daybreak, like the sun when it shines forth from on high at dawn and its light is not darkened, like rain when it makes green things spring up from the earth,
is it not indeed so? For he has made an everlasting covenant with me, for my deliverance and rescue up to this time, for everyone who attacks me is not pleasing to him.
For all that spring up like thorns and other things, like all the snuffings [?] of a candle — for no one touches them with a hand and plucks them out,
but with iron and wood. And they will all be burned with fire and consumed in their shame.
These are the names of the chiefs and commanders of David: Jezbal, son of Thekemenai, chief, the first of the three; he adorned [?] the provisions [?] over the nine hundred slain at one time.
After him was Eleazar, son of Dodo, among the three commanders; he was with David at Meseran [?], and the Philistines had gathered there for battle.

And at that place the Israelites came up early [?] among them, and he went out against them and met them face to face, and he struck down the Philistines until his hand grew weary, and the hilt of his sword stuck to his hand; and the Lord brought about a great salvation for the people on that day. And all the people returned to the plunder and spoil of the enemies.
After him was Shammah, son of Elah, of Rakean [?]; and the Philistines gathered for battle, and there was a field sown with lentils there, and the people fled from the Philistines.

And they came into the middle of the sown lentil field, and these men went out against them, struck them, and slaughtered the foreigners. And the Lord brought about a great deliverance among the people on that day.
And three men from David's three companies came to the cave at the rock of Adullam. The hostile foreigners had come and were encamped in the valley of the Titans.
And David was standing beside the face of the rock, and the bands of the foreigners were in Bethlehem at that very time.

And David was seized with longing and said: "Who will give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, the one by the gates?" And at that very time the band of the foreigners had surrounded Bethlehem.

And the three men who had come down from David's companies broke through the camp of the foreigners and brought him water from the well of Bethlehem, the one by the gates. But David did not want to drink the water. Instead he took it and poured it out before the Lord.

And he said: "The Lord forbid that I should do this, that I should drink the blood and the lives of these men along with this water!" And he would not drink the water. These are the things the three mighty men did before David.
And Abishai, the brother of Joab, chief among the three, stood out for his valour before David. In a single encounter he struck down [?] six hundred mighty men before David.
This one of the three was so much better and more renowned than the other two that he was their chief, but he did not equal the Three.

And Benaiah son of Jehoiada, son of Iessai [?], did many deeds, more than the man of Gabarael [Kabzeel], for he slew the two sons of Ariel of Moab. And he went down and killed the lion in the pit in the days of winter.

And he killed the Egyptian, a terrifying and powerful man whom no one could withstand. The Egyptian held a spear in his hands, and the shaft of his spear was like the beam of a bridge. The Egyptian came out against him with that spear, and Benaiah went to meet him. He took the spear away from the Egyptian and ran him through with his own spear.
These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and his name was the most distinguished among the three mighty men.
And he was more renowned than they were, but he did not equal the Three. And David set him over all the [?] (those summoned / the guard). And these are the names of David's mighty men:
Asahel, the brother of Joab, among the Thirty; Elhanan son of Dodo, of the city of Bethlehem;
Shammah the Daralite [?]; Kales [?] the Mphalmunite [?];
Idae son of Ekea, the Tekoite;
Abiezer the Anathothite; Sabee the Ketelite [?];
Eliman the Akakite [?]; Malnan the Peltelite [?];
Alan son of Abaan; One son of Phath; Lethi son of Eribai, who was from the hill of Benjamin;
Ade, who was from Ekabith [?];
Talsabe the Sarebathite; Azelmon the Akirnite;
Aldad the Salaminite; Iases the Gigunite [?]; Jonathan son of Samai; Araki son of Sakarua;
Arerima son of Phelet, son of Ozias;
Markathi the Atalamite; Ahithophel the Gileadite;
Miesiril [?] the Carmelite; the Apharian [?];
Joel, the brother of Nathan; Samaba son of Ager;
Salaad of Anam [?], Area the Beerothite, who carried Joab's armour,
and Ioath, Jether, Gamer, Iesther [?],
and Uriah the Hittite. All of these were thirty-seven men.
And the Lord's anger was kindled again against Israel, and he stirred up David against them, saying: Go, number for me all Israel and Judah.

And the king said to Joab and to the commander of the people who were with him in Jerusalem: Go and travel through the whole house of Israel and of Judah, from Dan to Beersheba. Count and number all the people, and bring me a written register of all the people, so that I may know the number of all the people together, how many there are.

Joab answered the king and said: May the Lord their God add to the people a hundred times as many as there are, and may my lord the king see it with his own eyes! But why has my lord the king set his heart on this plan, to do this thing?

But the king's command prevailed over Joab's word and over all the commanders of his army. And Joab and all the commanders went out from the king's presence to survey and register all the people of Israel.
And they went and crossed the Jordan, and they began from the city of Aroer, which lies between the valleys of Gad and Jazer.
They came to Gilead and to the land of Ketem and of Kadesh, and they came as far as Dan and drew near to all Sidon.
And they came to Bosor and to Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites, and they turned to the southern part of Judah, to Beersheba.
And they went through the whole land and arrived at Jerusalem in the ninth month, on the twentieth day.

And Joab brought the book of the land's census, full of figures, and laid it before the king. The number of the people of Israel was about nine hundred thousand armed men, and of Judah, chosen armed men, four hundred thousand armed men.

And David's heart was troubled because of the census of the people. David began to speak to the Lord and said: I have sinned greatly before the Lord in doing this thing. And now, O Lord, forgive this sin of your servant, for I have made this plan foolishly and to no purpose!
And when David rose in the morning, the word of the Lord came to David through Gad the prophet, saying:
Thus says the Lord: I will bring these three things upon you. Choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.

And Gad came to David and said to him: Choose for yourself one of these that I will bring upon you, and I will do it to you. The Lord has said: either three years of famine on the face of the land, or three months of fleeing before your enemies while they pursue you without respite, or three days of death among the people in your land. Now consider, understand, and answer me what I shall reply to the one who sent me.

David answered Gad and said: All three of these press very hard on me from every side. But it is better to fall into the hands of the Lord, for the compassion of his mercy is great, and let me not fall into the hands of men!

So David chose death among the people. It was the time of the wheat harvest. And the Lord sent death upon Israel from morning until the sixth hour. The plague came upon the people, and from Dan to Beersheba seventy-seven thousand men of the people fell.

And the angel, the bringer of death and the destroyer, stretched out his hand over Israel to kill it. And the Lord repented of that evil done to them, and said to the angel who was destroying the people: "It is enough; hold back your hand from now on!" And the angel was standing at the edge of the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

David began to speak to the Lord, for he saw the angel who had come down and was destroying the people of Israel, and he said: "Here I am, Lord, this shepherd who has sinned and done evil; but these sheep, what have they sinned? Let your hand be upon me and upon my father's house."
And Gad, David's prophet, came and said to him: "Go out quickly and set up an altar on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite!"
And David went out at the command of the prophet, as the Lord had commanded him.
And when Araunah saw that the king had set out and was coming toward him, with all his company behind him, Araunah went out to meet him and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.

And he said: "What is it, lord, what is it, king? Why do you come to your servant?" And David said to him: "I have come to buy this threshing floor from you and to build on it an altar to the Lord God, so that this plague may cease from this people!"

Araunah answered David and said to him: "Let my lord the king take it and do according to the command of the Lord God, as is pleasing to him! See, here are the oxen for sacrifice, and the yoke, and the plough, and all the threshing-floor implements for wood for the whole burnt offerings!"
"And may the Lord accept them with favour from your hands!"

The king answered and said: "Not so, as if I would take it for free; rather, I will pay you its price and offer these sacrifices to the Lord God, and I will not take it for free!" And David acquired the threshing floor by purchase, and the oxen for a price of fifty shekels of silver by weight.

And David built an altar to the Lord there and offered those sacrifices as peace offerings to the Lord God. Later Solomon added to it and enlarged that altar, for at first it was small. And the Lord was reconciled with the land, and the plagues ceased from Israel.
